title: Internal Mobility & Benefits Operations Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This playbook combines guidance on internal mobility (moves, promotions, and role transitions) with the operational details that make benefits and onboarding predictable and fast. It is intended for managers, people-ops partners, hiring managers, and HR operations to run consistent, fair transitions and ensure new joiners and movers receive timely benefits and tooling access.

1) Purpose and Scope
- Purpose: Reduce variance in internal transfers and benefits provisioning, shorten time-to-productivity for movers and new hires, and align promotion decisions to a shared rubric.
- Scope: Applies to all full-time employees and long-term contractors; covers lateral moves, promotions, role changes, exits, benefits enrollment, and core onboarding workflows. Does NOT replace team-level performance conversations or legal contract changes (finance/legal owned).

2) Principles
- Transparency: publish role expectations and promotion rubrics publicly on the People Portal.
- Timeliness: target 7 business days for access provisioning after an accepted transfer/promotion; target 30 days for compensation changes to be reflected in payroll cycles.
- Fairness: calibration across functions by quarterly review cycles with people-ops and department leads.
- Employee-first: minimize blocker work for the individual moving teams; prioritize uninterrupted productivity.

3) Internal Mobility: Types and Process
A. Types of moves
1. Lateral transfer: change of team/title without level change.
2. Promotion: level increase (IC or Manager path).
3. Dual-role / temporary matrix assignment: short-term project-based assignments.

B. Candidate-initiated vs. Manager-initiated
- Candidate-initiated: employee applies via Internal Job Board; manager of receiving team must complete a short-form intake in the People Portal and schedule interviews within 7 business days.
- Manager-initiated: originating manager opens a transfer request; people-ops validates role fit and suggests timeline.

C. Interview loop (standard, 3–4 steps)
1. Intro screen (15–30 min) — hiring manager: focus on role fit and expectations.
2. Technical/functional interviews (1–2 interviews, 45–60 min) — peers: focus on skills and working style.
3. Leadership/peer alignment (30–45 min) — cross-team questions, collaboration examples.
4. Offer & mobility approval — hiring manager + people-ops sign-off; compensation changes routed to Finance.

D. Timelines and SLAs
- Job posting -> first interview: 7 business days target.
- Final decision -> transfer start date: 10 business days target (exceptions for business-critical timing).
- Access and tooling provisioning: complete within 7 business days of start date.

4) Promotion & Leveling Rubric (summary)
- We publish full level profiles on the People Portal; below is the operational summary used in calibration panels. Each promotion decision should reference measurable examples across these dimensions:
  - Impact: demonstrable product/customer outcomes or technical/operational improvements with metrics.
  - Ownership: scope of work, independent project leadership, cross-team coordination.
  - Craft: depth of technical/product craft, decision clarity, quality of deliverables.
  - Mentorship & Collaboration: active coaching/mentorship, influence without authority.
  - Execution: reliability, velocity, and ability to unblock complex deliveries.

Promotion panel composition: hiring manager + previous manager (if applicable) + people-ops partner + cross-functional peer reviewer.

5) Compensation Operations (high level)
- Banding: every role is mapped to a compensation band; band ranges are market-derived and updated annually by People Ops + Finance.
- Review cadence: annual merit cycle in October; ad-hoc market adjustments possible with VP approval.
- Equity refreshes: eligibility at 24 months (standard) or at promotion.
- Pay timing: eligible changes approved before payroll cutoff result in the next monthly payroll; otherwise the following month.

6) Benefits & Perks: Enrollment and Operational Notes
- Core benefits: medical/dental/vision (enrollment window: 30 days from start), 14-week paid parental leave (primary), 6-week paid parental leave (secondary), mental health stipend ($360/year), flexible learning stipend ($1,200/year).
- Sabbatical: eligibility at 36 months; request process: submit a Sabbatical Petition form to people-ops 120 days before intended leave.
- Wellbeing: quarterly wellness days and company-sponsored mental health sessions scheduled by People Ops.
- Commuter & home-office: one-time home office stipend ($800 on new hire milestones) and commuter pre-tax benefit in supported regions.
- Benefits Exception Process: manager + people-ops to submit a Benefits Exception Request; Finance/legal must approve cost > $10k per year.

7) New Hire and Transition Checklist (operational runbook)
A. Pre-boarding (people-ops) — 7–14 days before start
- Create employee record in HRIS and assign employee ID.
- Send offer paperwork and benefits enrollment links.
- Create placeholder accounts in AccessManager for repos, Slack, email (provision on day 1).
- Ship welcome kit: laptop, charger, onboarding guide, and welcome swag (ship 5 business days before start).

B. Day 1 (manager + IT)
- Welcome meeting (30 min) with manager: role context, team norms, 30/60/90 goals.
- IT handoff: verify laptop, VPN, and key tooling access.
- HR intro: benefits demo and payroll setup.

C. First 30 days (manager + buddy + people-ops)
- Weekly check-ins with manager (first 4 weeks).
- Scheduled buddy sessions for product and infrastructure orientation.
- Complete core trainings: security, code of conduct, and data handling.

D. First 90 days (manager)
- Performance checkpoint at 30 and 90 days.
- Goal alignment and first small impact deliverable.

8) Tooling & Access (owners and onboarding steps)
- People Portal (People Ops): job postings, transfer requests, benefits forms. Owner: people-ops.
- AccessManager (IAM): requests for repo, cloud, and production access. Owner: Eng Security. Workflow: submit an access request ticket with manager approval; expect 48–72 hours for standard, 7 days for privileged production access.
- DevSpace (repos and CI): provisioned by eng-platform on first active repo commit. Owner: eng-platform.
- Redwood Console (product-facing operational dashboard): team owners must add new member via team settings; cross-org viewers given read-only by default.
- OnboardKit (task tracker for new hires): auto-populates manager and new hire tasks; People Ops owns template updates.

9) Role Handoffs and Knowledge Transfer Checklist (for movers)
- Document: open-source roadmap items, runbooks, DRI list, active tickets, and recurring meetings.
- Pairing: two-week co-delivery period with overlap where feasible.
- Access: origin manager to maintain access for 7 days post-transition for escalations.

10) Exceptional Flows
- Rapid redeployment: for business-critical reassignments, people-ops will fast-track access in 48 hours and waive standard posting timelines.
- Cross-border transfers: consult Finance and Legal for visa/payroll changes; expect 30–90 day lead time.

11) Ownership and Escalation
- People-ops: program owner for mobility and benefits operations (email: people-ops@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: unresolved cases escalate to Head of People within 5 business days.

12) Templates and Attachments (available on People Portal)
- Transfer intake form (fillable).
- Promotion case packet template.
- Benefits exception request form.

13) FAQ (short)
- Q: How long until my new manager assigns me work?
  A: Within 3 business days of official transfer start.
- Q: When will my benefits start?
  A: Benefits enrollment window opens immediately on start; coverage effective the first of the following month unless otherwise specified.
- Q: Who signs off promotions?
  A: Hiring manager + people-ops + cross-functional reviewer + VP (if band/level change requires budget).

14) Related pages

- Internal Job Board: /people-portal/internal-jobs
